metadata.summary: When the Jacksonville Jaguars selected Trevor Lawrence with the first overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, they were looking for a franchise saviour.
metadata.content: Trevor Lawrence: Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback finally hitting lofty heights expected from former No 1 overall pick | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Trevor Lawrence: Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback finally hitting lofty heights expected from former No 1 overall pick Trevor Lawrence was the No 1 overall NFL Draft pick in 2021 and has helped Jacksonville Jaguars become Super Bowl contenders after a rocky start to his career; watch Jaguars vs Texans at Wembley live on Sky Sports from 2pm on Sunday By James Simpson Thursday 15 October 2026 10:47, UK Image: Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence is playing the best football of his career When the Jacksonville Jaguars selected Trevor Lawrence with the first overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, they were looking for a franchise saviour. The Jags were coming off a 1-15 season, and an astonishing 11 losing campaigns out of the previous 13. They are one of just four teams in the NFL to have never played in a Super Bowl. Conversely, Lawrence arrived having won 34 of his 36 games in college and 52 of 54 in high school. He was supposed to bring those wins to Florida. messages.text: Martinez releases statement to clarify outburst - but does not apologise

metadata.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology.
metadata.content: Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender releases statement to clarify outburst but does not apologise | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender releases statement to clarify outburst but does not apologise Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy after their Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox Thursday 15 October 2026 06:15, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daily Mail’s Craig Hope and John Cross from The Mirror give their views on Lisandro Martinez's statement Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology. Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox. But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments.
